result.description: GTM data enrichment and prospecting platform; Public API runs searches, routines, tables, audiences, signals, workflows.
result.auth_detail: Personal API key in `clay-api-key` header, tied to user and workspace. Create via UI (API and CLI → API keys) or `clay api-keys create`. No OAuth documented for third-party apps (rate-limits page mentions "OAuth credentials" in passing).
result.access_detail: Per Clay University, developer platform available on all plans incl. Free and trial. Plan limits: search results per request/year scale by plan; structured table queries (Tables) are Enterprise only. Rate limit 300 req/min per workspace. Docs themselves don't state plan gating; the all-plans claim comes from Clay University.
result.api_notes: Base https://api.clay.com/public/v0, OpenAPI at developers.clay.com/openapi.json. Resources: Searches (companies/people), Routines (batch runs, JSONL), Tables (Enterprise), Audiences, Signals, Workflows (alpha), Credits, Me, Webhooks. Also a clay CLI and agent plugin. Table row reads and enrichment-by-table are limited; not a classic full CRUD of Clay tables on non-Enterprise.
result.blocker: Caveats: API is new (beta/alpha parts), table access Enterprise-only, search credit/volume limits by plan, API-key only (no OAuth for end users). Official MCP exists per docs but no dedicated setup/URL page found; mcp.clay.earth is a different product (Clay personal CRM).

evidence.quote: Every request to the Clay Public API must include a Clay API key in the `clay-api-key` header.
There are two ways to use Clay as a developer: install the agent plugin to build with Clay inside your coding agent, or call the Public API directly from your own applications and services.
Find companies and people in Clay's proprietary GTM database.
Use MCP to call Clay functions from a coding agent like Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor.
The developer platform is available across all Clay plans, including free and trial plans.
The default limit is **300 requests per minute per workspace** (about 5 requests per second), shared across all API keys and OAuth credentials in the workspace.
